messages:
devon: heads-up — i'm putting together a small playbook for runtime kernel-path probing across A100 / H100 / L4. want a quick sanity check before i file a follow-up RFC :eyes:
sara: love it. what are we prioritizing — perf, correctness, or stability?
mike: all three but order matters. correctness > stability > perf for prod rollouts. microbench probes can catch perf regressions early.
dan: (typo) — ignore
devon: yeah correctness first. main problem we keep hitting: capability bits from driver/SM are sometimes incomplete (esp on some L4 images). if we only trust CPUID-like flags we pick a kernel that later misbehaves. so probe must be behavioral, not just bit checks.
anita: behavioral probe = good. prefer safe fallback path over speculative fast kernels when uncertain. a 10-20% perf loss is acceptable vs silent corruption. :100: 
mike: FWIW we saw an L4 fleet board that reported tensor cores but had lower math throughput on fused attention. result: token-level tail spikes at scale.
lee: proposed playbook (short):
  1) capability bits quick-check (driver flags)
  2) microbench probe (local warmup, 5-10 runs, short seqs: 128/512) -> measure op throughput + correctness by comparing logits against reference FP32 baseline
  3) sampled in-prod validation (opsampler: 0.1-1% traffic) for 24-72h to catch stability/tail issues
  4) rollout with gradual canary + automatic fallback if kernel errors or >X% latency/regressions 

devon: agree. microbench should include attention kernels (causal, kv-cache path), matmul, and softmax numerics. also check memory allocator alignment behaviours for L4 (we had 64-byte vs 256-byte differences).
sara: what flags/metrics do we record to drive automatic fallback?
devon: minimal set: p50/p95 token latency, token-timings stddev, kernel exceptions count, divergence metric vs reference (L2 norm on logits or top-k agreement), OOM events, retry rates. thresholds: latency p95 > baseline*1.4 OR divergence L2 > 1e-3 -> trigger rollback/fallback. these are draft numbers.
anita: please include an explicit safety flag so ops can force all traffic to safe-path (runtime.gpu.force_safe=true). also add a diagnostic dump on fallback to S3 with kernel binary + params.
lee: small config snippet for the probe (for the runtime config store):
```json
{"probe_version":"v1","probe_steps":[{"name":"capcheck","timeout_ms":200},{"name":"microbench","runs":10,"seqs":[128,512],"compare_to":"fp32_ref"},{"name":"opsampler","rate":0.005,"duration_h":72}],"fallback_policy":{"on_error":"safe_kernel","on_latency_regress":true,"latency_factor":1.4,"divergence_threshold":0.001}}
```

mike: + add kernel timeouts and soft-kill of long-running kernels. L4 sometimes needs longer single-kernel runtime due to async copy patterns — so absolute ms timeouts should be adaptive by kernel type.

devon: good call. adaptive timeout = baseline * kernel_timeout_multiplier[kernel_type]. default multiplier 1.5.

infra-bot: deploying probe job: runtime.gpu.path_probe playbook v1 -> canary 0.5% on prod starting now. track: infra.telemetry.gpu_probe.*

sara: what about quantized kernels (4-bit/8-bit)? they can change numerical behavior; do we run separate probes?
anita: yes separate probe profiles per quantization config. also add per-model prompt-length distribution sampling; quant buckets can amplify small numeric diffs.

lee: open questions we should capture in the RFC follow-up:
  - how long to keep opsampler running to detect flaky HW vs one-off blips (24h vs 72h)
  - storage format for kernel diagnostics (symbols + perf counters + input/seed)
  - can we unify microbench harness across clouds (driver differences)?
  - telemetry quotas: how much opsampler traffic can we afford in heavy production?

mike: my suggestion: 72h opsampler by default, allow rookies to shorten to 24h for faster iteration. diagnostics format: tarball of kernel .o + perf counters JSON + small input trace.
devon: i'll iterate and open the RFC follow-up with the playbook + config above + proposed thresholds. for now action items:
  - infra: validate probe job and telemetry streams (infra@)
  - eng-runtime: implement adaptive timeout and safe-path flag (devon + lee)
  - eng-ml: craft FP32 reference set for attention kernels (mike + anita)
  - ops: prepare rollback runbook and S3 bucket for diagnostics (sara)

anita: happy to own FP32 refs. will pick 10 models spanning small->large and sequences 64/128/512.

infra-bot: note: probe job created 1718209921, job-id=probe-2024-11-13-07

sara: LGTM. devon file the RFC when you have the draft — we'll triage in architecture meeting on weds. :white_check_mark:
